## Update 1

Every region is set to layer 1 only.  
The orange box is a `NavigationMeshAreaBox3D` that has layer 2 toggled:  
Therefore, if the agent's path query has layer 2 toggled, it will be affected by the changed cost. If it's not toggled, it stays unaffected.  
So a lava monster can walk on lava (layer 2), but some random NPC would rather walk around it. Unless there's only lava - or worse.

More testing will continue another time.

Still wondering about that mono pipeline issue, though.

https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/f82a6d2e-31de-4191-99a5-3d88398f2f79

## Update 2

Creating areas using just server works as well (just no debug gizmo rendering, yet):


https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/e6fbda7d-0245-4130-a046-7f96470485bb


## Update 3

done
* Server-only works
  * will not support scaling in server until valid demand arises
  * Gizmos are not possible, because they're editor-only. They'd need to be on server side (quite a big change). Face coloring in normal debug is not possible, because there's no area identification in the `NavigationMesh`.

bugs
* [x] cylinder gizmo: using the handlers for heights sets the radius to `0.0` (and vice versa)
  * API changed; or was broken in original PR
* [x] debug face coloring does not work if `!enabled_geometry_face_random_color.` in build

todo
* [x] changing the navigation layer of an area at runtime
* [x] more testing in test server

ideas
* [x] for query speed-up: if we cache the navigation layers indices we're actually interested in, then we can shorten for-loops, most notably the cost lookup
* ~~memory saving potential in `ProjectedArea`, or is it overkill?~~
  * saving one float per area (that's only needed for baking) is deemed overkill, for now

to be discussed
* [x] if an area overwrites the navigation layers, which cost should be used?
  * **the highest**
  * ~~the lowest?~~
  * ~~the first matching layer starting at the beginning?~~
    * (as far as I could tell, this was the way in the original PR, even though the description said otherwise)

scrapped
* rotation support when using server
  * is part of baking process. makes no sense

## Update on area navigation layers update during runtime **EDIT**: a `EditorInspectorPlugin` should do it **EDIT 2**: will try `_get_property_list` approach first problem: there's just no sane way to keep the area mesh _nodes_ connected to a region/navmesh after the baking is done. areas can be baked to multiple regions, making it unreasonable to save anything inside areas, especially given that you can throw away a region's navmesh anytime… Even if it's implemented in some way, editing one area node could update multiple regions. Or we could limit the area to the last region it was baked to, but then again… Either way, lots of potential for frustration and confusion solution: in short: just don't. leave the nodes for baking. show a region-area gui editor when a region is selected: what changes * no special treatment for area nodes to make runtime changes of navigation layers work * _no need_ for RIDs, at all. we already have permanent IDs, saved to the baked navmesh * region gets dirty directly, instead of some roundabout way when using just the server (mostly done, and I can delete some code) * area definitions/setup only via source geometry resource (`NavigationMeshSourceGeometryData3D`) * the resource creates some IDs unique to the resource, _and therefore_ unique to the navmesh * the IDs can be used to update navigation layers; sth. like `NavigationServer3D::set_area_navigation_layers(region_rid, area_id, layers)` * once a navigation mesh is set/loaded, automatically collect the areas from the navmesh resource and register them on the nav server inside `NavRegion3D` when using nodes and the editor, use `_get_property_list` logic. If this fails, show a new `EditorInspectorPlugin`: * looks similar to `EditorPropertyLayers`+`EditorPropertyArray`, generated when using `@export_flags_3d_navigation var test: PackedInt32Array` in a script * when the flags equal the region's config, the area is considered disabled. maybe add a convenience "disable"-button that auto-sets the areas flags to the region's * instead of a grab button to reorder array items, add a focus button. to move the camera to that spot (lookat-logic) * or better: make it a "select"-button. a selection changes the color of the debug mesh faces. focus can be done in a second button * instead of numbers 0..x, give pseudo names that include shape type and the id: "Box::1", "Cylinder::2" * no: delete button, "add element". because everything is already baked * above everything, show layers of region (for reference) * add an "area"-picker. pick an area in the 3d editor. if a match is found, auto-scroll in editor to the correct entry and highlight it (briefly by blinking) and some convenience code to use an area node as reference to find the matching baked area inside a region. using AABB and approximately equal logic. **STATE**: is already editable in inspector. not affecting map sync yet
